title: Take the guided tour | Verse Engine by Ctruh
description: Take the guided tour in the Verse Engine by Ctruh docs: what it is, how to use it, and where it fits in your 3D workflow.

docs.article:
Take the guided tour#

Every page of Verse has a guided tour: the product page, the app, Studio and these docs. It points at the real controls, one at a time, and says in a sentence or two what each one does. Several steps ask you to try the control yourself (drag the scene, press Walk) and move on when you have.

You need: nothing. No account, no upload. The app tour loads a demo scene for you.

Start it#

  • First visit: a small invitation appears on the page: "New here? Take the 2-minute tour". Click it to start, or close it; it does not come back once dismissed.
  • Any time: the Tour entry in the navigation of every page opens the chapter list. Start from the beginning, resume where you stopped, or jump straight to a chapter such as "Uploading your model".
  • By link: add ?guide=<surface> to a page address. The surfaces are app, studio and docs; the product page uses /#guide=landing (a query on / opens the app). A chapter or step id after a colon opens the tour there.
LinkOpens
/#guide=landingThe product tour, from the top
/app?guide=appThe app tour, from the top
/app?guide=app:uploadThe app tour at "Uploading your model"
/studio?guide=studioThe Studio tour
/docs/?guide=docsThe docs tour
any page with ?guide=0No chip and no tour on that visit

Nothing ever opens by itself. The tour does not appear inside an embedded viewer. (?tour= is a different thing: in the app it plays a recorded camera tour.)

Chapters#

Use these ids after the colon, or pick the chapter from the list.

PageChapter ids
Product page (landing)what · how · features · start
App (app)scene · navigate · walk · auto-tour · review · export · quality · share · upload
Studio (studio)account · library · sharing
Docs (docs)navigate · guides · reference · news

From code, window.verseOnboarding.start("app", "upload") does the same thing, and window.verseOnboarding.chapters("app") lists them.

Move through it#

ControlDoes
Next or the right arrow keyNext step
Back or the left arrow keyPrevious step
Skip, the close button, or EscClose the tour; your place is remembered
The list button in the panelChapter list: jump anywhere

A step marked Try it waits for you to use the highlighted control and then advances. You can always press Next instead. While you are in walk mode the arrow keys belong to walking, so use the buttons there.

What each tour covers#

  • Product page: what Verse is, the live demo, how a file becomes a link, what you can do with one, and where to start. Its last step opens the app and the tour carries on there.
  • App: loading a demo scene; orbit, zoom and keyboard control; the measure tool; walk mode and the floor-plan minimap; the automatic camera tour; review comments; video export; quality options; sharing; and uploading your own model, with the formats and limits read from the server.
  • Studio: the account token, your scene library and its numbers, unlisted and private visibility, per-person share links, embed snippets, deleting and claiming scenes.
  • Docs: the sidebar and search, the how-to guides, the exporters for Blender, Unity and Unreal, the API, the changelog and the blog.

If a control is not on the page (the outline column on a narrow screen, for example) the tour skips that step rather than point at nothing.

What it stores and sends#

Progress is kept in your browser's local storage under the key verse-onboarding: which step you reached on each page, whether you finished, and whether you closed the chip. Clear it to see the chip again. Nothing about you is stored on the server.

The tour reports four anonymous events through the same telemetry channel the viewer uses: started, furthest step reached, completed, and skipped at step N. Each carries the page name and the step id only. See the telemetry schema.

Related#

  • Getting started covers the same ground as the app tour, in writing.
  • Collect client review comments, Export a flythrough video and Share privately with tokens go deeper on the features the tour introduces.
